newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 90 +1 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 136 n/c on last week

@ AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle exhibited a slightly weaker tone this week. For Australian cattle producers and beef processors, probably the most significant news of the week was to be found in the latest USDA cattle on feed (COF) statistics. Although trends depicted by the August COF report were expected, analysts were caught off guard by the extent of the changes.

In Korea over the past three weeks, the distribution of beef has been building up prior to the four day Chusok thanksgiving (26-29 Sept). This holiday is a traditional time for Koreans to celebrate the end of the harvest and to travel back to their original farming lands.
Due to the increasing beef demand and rising prices prior to Chusok, the LPMO has been releasing increased quantities of beef onto the wholesale market in order to help stabilise.

In the U.S. fedlots during August were a lot higher than expected and cattle marketings out of US fedlots were at the low end of estimates. The higher placements and lower marketings meant that the number of cattle in US feedlots is now only eight percent below last year, compared to 15 percent below in July.

U.S. domestic lean grinding beef prices moved high late this week, the combined result of fewer cows coming onto the market and improvement demand. The imported beef trade was very quiet, primarily because many participants are in Toronto for the American Meant Institue and Meat Importers Council of America's annual convention.
Japan this week focused on the strength of wholesale markets. Chilled Australian beef is in short supply following the decline in imports in August and September.
Wholesale prices for chilled grassfed and grainfed beef continued to rise with some prices returning to pre-BSE and E. coli levels.
